Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English. As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,

I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position at Adolescent Wellness Academy as I believe my extensive experience in adolescent mental health and behavioral health operations aligns perfectly with your needs. With over five years of leadership experience in clinical settings, I have successfully supervised multidisciplinary teams and managed programs focused on delivering high-quality care to adolescents and families.

In my current role as Clinical Director at Hope Haven Inc., I oversee a team of approximately 20 staff members, ensuring compliance with CARF standards while fostering a trauma-informed environment. My background includes developing treatment plans, conducting crisis interventions, and maintaining documentation quality, which are crucial for the success of your new facility in North Carolina. Additionally, my experience with intensive outpatient programs has equipped me with the skills necessary to enhance client outcomes and employee experiences, aligning with your commitment to clinical excellence and a supportive workplace culture.

I am particularly drawn to your values of kindness, growth, and optimism, which resonate with my leadership philosophy. I am eager to contribute to the launch and ongoing success of your clinic, ensuring that we not only meet but exceed the expectations of the adolescents and families we serve.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and vision can support the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.

Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position with your PHP and IOP programs. As an art educator, experienced teacher, and graduate student in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a specialization in Play Therapy, I have built my career around exactly what this role describes: using creative, process-based experiences to help young people express themselves, regulate their emotions, and discover their own capacity to grow.

Over the past couple of years, I have taught process-based art to children and adolescents in a variety of settings. At artNEST Studios, I facilitated weekly after-school art programs for elementary students, designing curriculum that intentionally prioritized creative exploration over the final product. This approach gives participants permission to take risks, make mistakes, and express themselves authentically. I also managed full-cycle logistics for camps, workshops, and parties, adapting programming in real time to different group dynamics, ability levels, and unexpected challenges while maintaining safety standards. These experiences taught me how to read the room, keep a group engaged, and create a warm, inclusive environment where participants feel safe to participate fully.

My work extends beyond the art studio into clinical and crisis contexts. I served as a Volunteer Crisis Counselor with The Trevor Project, providing culturally competent crisis support to LGBTQ+ youth, and I currently volunteer with Harmonia, where my training in crisis de-escalation, harm reduction, and trauma-informed care allows me to provide on-site emotional support to individuals experiencing acute psychological distress.

What draws me most to AWA is the belief that growth happens through connection, creativity, and kindness. I have seen firsthand how a safe space to create can open the door to emotional expression for young people who struggle to put their feelings into words. I would be honored to bring my experience in art facilitation, group management, and trauma-informed support to adolescents in your program, and I can offer consistent weekly or biweekly availability for on-site groups.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my creative practice and clinical training can contribute to your organization.

Warm regards,
Natalia Perez

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

candidates.summary:
I am a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults in educational, recreational, and community-based settings.

My clinical experience includes providing individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health and working with adolescents and young adults at Family First and New Directions for Young Adults. In these settings, I have supported clients experiencing anxiety, depression, emotional dysregulation, interpersonal challenges, neurodivergence, identity development, and life transitions. My experience includes individual counseling, therapeutic group facilitation, treatment planning, risk assessment, safety planning, and collaboration with clinical teams.

I have developed and facilitated experiential therapeutic groups incorporating DBT skills, interpersonal effectiveness, emotional regulation, mindfulness, creative expression, and adventure-based activities. My approach integrates Adlerian theory, CBT, DBT, Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions, with a strong emphasis on therapeutic relationships, belonging, encouragement, and personal growth.

Prior to entering the counseling profession, I spent more than 15 years in youth engagement, Jewish education, summer camps, and challenge course programming. These experiences strengthened my ability to build rapport with adolescents, facilitate meaningful group experiences, navigate challenging interpersonal dynamics, and create supportive environments that encourage self-discovery.

I also serve as an adjunct instructor at Lynn University and remain actively engaged in the therapeutic adventure and experiential education community. In fact, I am currently attending our annual international conference in Estes Park, Colorado, where I continue to connect with fellow professionals, exchange ideas, and explore innovative approaches to experiential learning and therapeutic practice. I bring a creative, collaborative, strengths-based approach to counseling and a passion for helping young people develop the skills, confidence, and connections necessary to thrive.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

A family calling a treatment program is usually scared, tired, and unsure what to ask. I have spent years being the calm person in that kind of moment, and I would like to bring that to Adolescent Wellness Academy as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator.

For five years I helped physical therapists with exercises and safe transfers in a skilled nursing facility. I also learned to explain things plainly, notice what someone needed before they said it, and pass the right details to the nursing team. As a peer mentor at UCF, I sat with students who felt lost and pointed them to the right next step, whether that was advising, research, or campus support. 

I never let a student leave without a plan. That is the same follow-through your callers need.
I also work well without close supervision. I completed my B.S. in Biomedical Sciences while running RT-qPCR and luciferase assays in a research lab and working shifts at Subway, where I handled 100+ orders a shift. I keep careful records, I take privacy seriously, and I stay organized when things get busy.

I am honest about where I am starting. I have not yet held a formal admissions role or worked remotely, and my Spanish is at an elementary level. I am a fast learner and eager to learn insurance verification and your intake process. I speak English and Romanian fluently and understand how much it means to hear a warm voice in a language you are comfortable with.

Thank you for your time. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can help your families take that first step.

Sincerely,
Alexis Cenadic

candidates.cover_letter:
To Whom It May Concern,
I am excited about this position because it combines many areas of administration that I enjoy. I hold a BA in Arts Administration with a minor in Business Administration from Elon University, and I am currently pursuing a Certificate in Nonprofit Management from Drexel University. I have worked in nonprofit organizations for my entire career and have a strong background in marketing, development, community engagement, and education.
I gained marketing experience from my position as the Marketing & Communications Specialist at the MetroWest Boston Visitors Bureau. At this position, I developed and implemented a comprehensive social media marketing strategy to increase followers and views on various platforms. I also created visually pleasing marketing materials for email campaigns, newsletters, and magazines. While working as the Marketing Coordinator at Burlington Academy of Dance & Arts, I managed the company’s website and email communications. I collaborated with partner organizations on various initiatives and helped create awareness of the organization in the community. Additionally, I have several years of experience creating marketing graphics and am skilled at using Canva. I am a strong writer and pride myself on my organizational skills. I have a robust understanding of how to utilize a strong brand image for an organization and have experience collaborating with various people to ensure cohesion in marketing materials. I have created various marketing calendars and am comfortable ensuring that campaigns stay on track. 
 I worked as the Grants Manager at Charlottesville Ballet and helped write grant applications for many different grantmaking bodies. I managed our application process from initial inquiry to receipt of payment and I ensured that we submitted all required materials for applications and reports. I used my strong writing skills to write grant application narratives, and used my project management skills to stay on top of each grant that we had in progress. I also collaborated with the development team to curate our donor list and connected with patrons at donor events. In this position, I used Salesforce as our CRM software to manage grant applications and donor profiles.
In my current community engagement role as the Springboard Fellow at North Carolina Hillel, I am responsible for planning and facilitating learning events and cohorts for college students. I develop education material and facilitate classes for students. I also handle the logistics of all events including renting spaces, communicating with vendors, and creating budgets. I also create all promotional material for our events and classes, including social media graphics, parent newsletters, and individual text outreach. I collaborate with my supervisor on developing and editing our social media and marketing strategies throughout the year to best promote our offerings and reach our intended audience. 
I am excited about this position and I look forward to discussing my relevant experience with you further. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Sophie Taylor

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over 10 years of administrative and healthcare experience, including direct experience in substance use treatment administration, patient coordination, and clinical operations, I believe I bring a strong combination of professional experience, compassion, and organizational skills to this position.

In my current role as an Administrative Field Trainer and Auditor with Denver Recovery Group, an outpatient medication-assisted treatment provider, I support multiple clinic locations and work closely with counselors, nurses, providers, and administrative teams. My responsibilities include coordinating patient intake processes, assisting with admissions and transfers, reviewing patient documentation, maintaining confidential records, communicating with patients and outside providers, and ensuring administrative requirements are completed accurately. I also have experience navigating healthcare systems, handling sensitive patient information, and helping individuals access treatment services.

In addition to my professional experience, I am currently pursuing my Master's Degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a focus on Addiction and Recovery at Capella University. My education has strengthened my understanding of mental health, substance use disorders, co-occurring conditions, trauma, and the importance of providing compassionate, person-centered care. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to support adolescents and adults who may be taking their first steps toward treatment and recovery.

I understand that the admissions process is often the first interaction a client or family has with a treatment program. That interaction can make a significant difference, especially when someone is reaching out during a difficult or overwhelming time. I believe in listening without judgment, communicating clearly, following up consistently, and helping individuals understand their options and next steps. I also bring strong attention to detail, experience with electronic healthcare systems, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining confidentiality and professionalism.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health experience, administrative background, and passion for helping others to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and career goals align with your programs.

Sincerely,
Dedra Ables

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my experience working in a hospital setting as a Unit Secretary, I have developed strong communication, organization, multitasking, and coordination skills that I believe would make me a valuable addition to your team.

I believe it is important to approach every interaction with patience, compassion, professionalism, and understanding. I would welcome the opportunity to help individuals and families feel heard, supported, and guided toward the next step in their care.

While my experience has primarily been in an in-person healthcare environment, I am comfortable working independently, managing responsibilities, learning new systems, and staying focused on completing tasks efficiently. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and dedication could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,

Lindsay

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. My professional background has centered on supporting individuals and families navigating difficult and often overwhelming circumstances, and I would welcome the opportunity to bring that experience to a team focused on helping individuals access the care and support they need.

In my previous role as an Outreach and Advocacy Coordinator at a Children's Advocacy Center, I worked closely with children and families experiencing crisis, often serving as an initial point of contact and helping them navigate available services and resources. My responsibilities included coordinating services with multidisciplinary partners, conducting forensic interviews, supervising and training victim advocates, and ensuring families were connected with appropriate support. This work required compassion, professionalism, strong communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage sensitive information with discretion.

I also have experience coordinating multiple responsibilities, maintaining documentation, managing follow-up, and building relationships with professionals across various organizations. Through my graduate studies in Conflict Management, I have further developed my skills in communication, conflict resolution, and navigating complex situations with empathy and professionalism.

I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an overwhelming first step for individuals and families. I believe my background in advocacy and client-centered support would allow me to approach these conversations with patience, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping callers feel heard and supported.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Caricia Zamora

Enid Baerga

November 18, 2026

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With my professional background in social services, case management, crisis intervention, and trauma-informed care, I believe I can bring both the experience and compassion needed to support individuals and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

Throughout my career, I have worked closely with individuals facing difficult life circumstances, including survivors of trauma, people experiencing emotional distress, and individuals navigating complex social service systems. My work with Real Escape From the Sex Trade (REST), along with my experience as a Community Resource Specialist and Case Manager, has taught me the importance of listening without judgment, identifying immediate needs, connecting individuals with appropriate resources, and following through to ensure they receive the support they deserve.

I also bring experience working remotely in healthcare-related customer service, particularly with Medicare and Medicaid members. This work strengthened my ability to communicate with healthcare providers, navigate insurance coverage, assist individuals in understanding their benefits, and manage sensitive information with professionalism and confidentiality.

As a bilingual English and Spanish professional, I understand how important it is for individuals and families to feel heard, respected, and understood, especially when reaching out for help during vulnerable moments. I believe that the first conversation can make a significant difference in someone's willingness to seek treatment. My approach has always been to meet people where they are, without judgment, while helping them identify practical steps toward receiving care.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to combine my experience in human services with my passion for helping people access meaningful support. I understand that admissions coordination requires more than answering calls or completing paperwork. It requires patience, empathy, organization, and the ability to build trust while guiding individuals through what can be an overwhelming process.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my skills and experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my professional background aligns with your team's mission.

Sincerely,

Enid Baerga

ebaerga@gmail.com

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in your Admissions position. This is very close to me since I have seen all of its sides from within. I was born and raised in the foster care system where I experienced firsthand what the problems related to addiction, mental health issues, trauma, and difficult living conditions can do to a person. I saw people struggling with all the things in their life and being ignored, misunderstood, and sometimes even judged because of what they have been through. It taught me to understand and appreciate people and not to judge anyone for the environment that he or she came from.

I also have experience of dealing with mental illness myself. As a child I fought against an eating disorder and battled my mental health, and my journey to recovery was the hardest thing I have ever done. This experience gave me much more understanding of resilience, vulnerability, and healing process than I can express in words. I know that healing takes time. I know that there are hard days when you cannot see any progress and that having someone by your side can make all the difference. 

Over the past 15 years I have managed to develop myself into someone who is immensely proud of their lifestyle since overcoming the disease. Not only have I become a mother, returned to education, completed my degree, but I am currently in the last stages of obtaining my Master's degree. I have been honored with being able to help my friends to overcome the same struggles. It was my experience which made me understand that our past cannot dictate our future. I would like to be able to utilize all my knowledge and help people see the possibility of achieving a brighter future. 

I have experience with admissions and administration as well as being organized, a great communicator, and possessing good interpersonal skills. I do really like helping people, relating to people, working with families, and being able to keep everything behind the scenes running smoothly. I understand that being admitted to a facility may be one of the most emotionally vulnerable experiences for someone seeking help, because I have been there. It may just be the simple act of hearing someone’s first voice, knowing that someone really cares, that makes all the difference.

What I am looking for is an environment in which I can combine my professional skills with my personal passion for helping people. I would like to be able to use my administrative and admissions skills for an organization that really does make a difference in people’s lives and allows me to continue growing.

I understand how it is like to come from tough conditions, to have one's personal struggles, and strive towards a better future. And maybe that is the reason why this piece of writing is so meaningful to me. For if my experience, my sympathy, or even just one contact could make anyone feel a little bit less lonely on their path, I would be very happy about being a part of that process.

I thank you for the time you take reading my application and making it this far in my letter!


Mahalo,

Tanya Diskant Abney

617-505-9932

Ada Rivera-Luciano

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

My career has run along two tracks that most people treat as separate: home care for people with developmental disabilities, and substance use services. To me they've always been the same work. Whether someone is learning to live more independently in a group home or rebuilding their life in recovery, the job is to meet them where they are, keep them safe, and help them take the next step on their own terms.

Working both sides has made me better at each. Home care taught me the daily fundamentals of support and how trust gets built over time. Substance use work taught me to stay steady in a crisis and to see the whole person behind a diagnosis or a behavior. A lot of the people we serve live where those worlds overlap, and I'm comfortable in that space.

This work is personal for me. I was raised by my great-grandmother because my parents and grandmother were in active addiction, and I know firsthand what it means when caring people show up for you. I've spent my career trying to be that person for others.

If you give me this opportunity, you'll gain someone reliable, calm under pressure, and genuinely invested in the people you serve. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Dom Daugherty

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I want to help people through a part of seeking care that can feel especially hard: making the first call. As a paraeducator with Aurora Public Schools and a Master of Social Work student at Metropolitan State University of Denver, I would bring experience working with families and a genuine interest in helping people access behavioral health care.

As an assistant director at Everbrook Academy, I used SproutAbout to keep families informed and maintain records across classrooms. I also helped coordinate staff schedules and onboarding. As a lead infant teacher at Primrose Schools, I spoke with families daily about their children’s routines and development. Those conversations taught me to ask what a caregiver is most concerned about, listen closely, and give a specific answer they can use.

In my social work coursework, I practice asking open-ended questions and checking that I have understood what someone wants to share. I would bring that approach to a parent calling Adolescent Wellness Academy about their teenager and to an adult contacting Principles Recovery Center about their own substance use. Before ending a call, I would confirm the next step with the caller and document it accurately so the colleague following up knows what the caller has already shared.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience with families and program operations could support your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Chloe Verdun

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With over six years of experience in behavioral health administration, patient intake, clinical coordination, and executive support, I believe I bring the professional experience, interpersonal skills, and compassionate approach necessary to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

In my previous role as Office Manager and Executive Assistant at Self Help Los Angeles, I gained extensive experience working directly with individuals navigating a wide range of mental health and behavioral health challenges. My responsibilities included conducting patient intakes and consultations, maintaining confidential clinical records, coordinating therapy appointments, documenting services, and ensuring that administrative processes were completed accurately and efficiently. I regularly worked with individuals experiencing a wide range of mental health and substance use challenges, which strengthened my ability to communicate with compassion, professionalism, and understanding.

 I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience, particularly for youths and parents seeking help for their children. I take pride in being approachable, attentive, and reassuring while maintaining appropriate professionalism and boundaries. I believe that making someone feel heard, respected, and comfortable during that first interaction can make a significant difference in their willingness to pursue treatment.

In addition to my direct patient-facing experience, I have a strong administrative and organizational background. My responsibilities included tracking office metrics, managing patient documentation, developing efficient filing systems, payroll, data entry, business marketing, social media management, website development through WordPress, and creating email campaigns through Infusionsoft. I am comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, maintaining accurate records, communicating with different stakeholders, and following through on tasks without sacrificing attention to detail. I understand the importance of confidentiality and accuracy when handling sensitive patient information.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my behavioral health background with my passion for helping individuals and families access the care they need. I would welcome the opportunity to be a supportive and knowledgeable first point of contact for prospective clients and their families, helping them navigate the admissions process with clarity, compassion, and confidence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, communication skills, and dedication to patient-centered care could benefit your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work your programs provide.

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. What immediately drew me to this opportunity was the emphasis on compassion, communication, and the understanding that the first person someone speaks with can significantly influence their willingness to seek help. I believe that individuals navigating mental health challenges or substance use disorders deserve to be met with dignity, patience, and understanding, especially when taking the difficult first step toward treatment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed strong skills in communication, conflict resolution, administrative coordination, and managing sensitive situations with professionalism and empathy. My experience in a supervisory role has strengthened my ability to remain composed under pressure, communicate effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds, maintain accurate documentation, and balance multiple responsibilities without sacrificing attention to detail. These experiences have taught me that successful communication requires more than simply providing information; it requires actively listening, recognizing individual needs, and helping people feel heard and respected.

My academic background in psychology has further strengthened my understanding of human behavior, mental health, and the influence that personal experiences and environmental circumstances can have on an individual’s well-being. Through my studies, I have developed a deeper appreciation for the complexities of psychological distress, trauma, and the importance of compassionate, individualized support. I am particularly interested in applying this knowledge in a position where I can help individuals and families navigate the often overwhelming process of seeking behavioral health treatment.

I recognize that effective admissions coordination requires both genuine compassion and exceptional organization. Whether answering inquiries, coordinating assessments, explaining treatment options, maintaining confidential records, or following up with prospective clients, I understand the importance of accuracy, consistency, discretion, and accountability. I am confident in my ability to learn new systems, manage competing priorities, and communicate clearly while maintaining the professionalism and sensitivity that healthcare environments demand.

What makes this opportunity especially meaningful to me is the possibility of being a reassuring presence during an incredibly vulnerable moment in someone’s life. I understand that behind every inquiry is a person or family seeking answers, reassurance, and hope. I would approach each interaction with the belief that no one should feel dismissed, judged, or overlooked when asking for help.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my communication skills, leadership experience, academic knowledge, and dedication to compassionate service to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and commitment to helping others align with the missions of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Dear hiring team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

My name is Emily, and I am writing to express my immense interest in your Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I have extensive experience in office management and administrative tasks in a hybrid mental health setting. In my most relevant position, I started as an administrative assistant to a Ph.D. in private practice before being promoted to office manager. Here, I was the sole source of communication for clients, clinicians, insurance companies, case managers, and the like. I did all general bookkeeping while also billing, hiring, scheduling, stocking, marketing, managing licensure, updating staff on changing laws, creating presentations, and more. No day in my position was the same. Though my job title did not directly reflect it, I also provided executive assistance to a Ph.D.  

I received my Bachelor of Science in Psychology from Arizona State University, and pursued coursework that not only taught me about chemical deficiencies and neurotransmitters, but also how to thrive in a stressful environment, how to self-regulate, how to empathize and listen, and how people are likely to react to our responses, professionalism, and character when greeted with different environmental stimuli. Hiring Team 
Adolescent Wellness Academy 

Re: Application for Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology, credentialing as a Behavior Technician, and extensive hands-on experience in child advocacy, victim support, and behavioral health, I am eager to serve as a compassionate, organized, and reassuring first point of contact for families navigating youth mental health and residential care.

Welcoming a child into a treatment or wellness program is often one of the most overwhelming decisions a parent or guardian can make. Through my background as a Court-Appointed Special Advocate (CASA), a shelter-based victim advocate, and a Certified Crisis Prevention Specialist, I have developed a calm, trauma-informed communication style tailored to high-stress situations. I excel at building immediate rapport with families, listening with genuine empathy, and translating complex clinical and administrative requirements into clear, manageable steps.

In addition to family engagement, my experience directly supports the operational demands of admissions coordination:


•	Clinical & Behavioral Alignment: As an RBT, I work closely with interdisciplinary teams, adhere strictly to HIPAA and documentation standards, and understand the nuances of behavioral assessments and individualized treatment planning. Allowing me to gather accurate clinical intake information and collaborate seamlessly with your clinical directors.

•	Advocacy & Crisis De-escalation: My work in shelter environments and child advocacy has equipped me to conduct thorough initial screenings, assess urgent safety or support needs, and guide families through difficult transitions with patience and dignity.

•	Administrative Precision & Follow-Through: Balancing high-volume case documentation, investigative reporting, and multi-agency coordination has honed my ability to manage inquiry pipelines, verify eligibility and insurance details accurately, and ensure no family falls through the cracks during the intake process.

As both a behavioral health professional and a parent, I deeply admire Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to holistic, evidence-based adolescent care. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical insight, advocacy background, and organizational dedication to your admissions team to help more young people and their families access the support they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my background aligns with your team's goals.

Sincerely,

Candace R. Hurd

My dad’s struggle with substance use began when he was 16, and I’ve seen other people I love struggle with it, too. Since my dad passed away, I’ve felt an even stronger pull toward work that helps people get care. I know what it’s like to love someone who’s struggling and feel unsure how to help. I volunteered with the VA’s behavioral health intake team and later worked closely with the CRC intake team on billing at Centene. As a supervisor at Maximus, I helped my team handle escalated cases and explain next steps to people who were frustrated or overwhelmed.
Whether I’m speaking with a parent worried about their teen or an adult seeking treatment, I’d take the time to hear their concerns, explain their options in plain language, and follow through on scheduling or a referral. I want families to know they can support someone they love without having to figure out treatment on their own.
Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to bring my experience and personal commitment to your admissions team.
Kind Regards,
Monique Alvarado

Letitia Ann Jacobs annjacobs253@gmail.com 832-914-9605

I’d like to express my interest in a career field that allows growth potential, as well as a position

sets, will contribute significantly to meeting or exceeding your company’s overall goals.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

I am drawn to this opportunity because it combines strong communication, organization, and client support with the ability to make meaningful connections and a difference in the lives of individuals and their families seeking care. 

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and vulnerable expereince. However, it is the hardest part of the entire process: asking for help. I believe the first interaction is essential because of the lasting impression it has on someone's healing experience. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I hope that this Cover Letter finds you and your loved ones in good health and good spirits. I find myself excited while typing this letter to you as I feel that the position of Virtual Admissions Coordinator with the Adolescent Wellness Academy is a great fit when I consider my professional and personal experiences as well as my goals for future growth and the needs of my family. Thank you for taking the time to read my cover letter, resume and application, and I hope that my sincere interest to join your team and help our community is clear.

I’ve highlighted a few accomplishments that you won’t find in my resume related to my leadership skills. I would be remiss if I did not mention my high school achievements. I was President of our National Honor Society, Cadet Commander of our Air Force Jr. ROTC, and participated in many other extracurricular activities. I was nominated for and awarded the New Jersey Association of Student Councils’ 2006 Student Leader of the Year Award. While attending Rutgers University (New Brunswick Campus) I elected to try out for their club ice hockey team after almost a 2-year hiatus from organized hockey and working through some personal issues related to mental health while attending county college. I made the ACHA D-II Men’s Ice Hockey team and after my first full season with the team, I was asked by our coach to be the team’s captain. As part of my studies, I interned with Ed Snider Youth Hockey & Education (Snider Hockey) during the summer of 2011. Over the course of 10 years, I was promoted to part-time Coach, Rink Coordinator, Senior Coordinator and eventually HR Manager. I would love the opportunity to continue to contribute my skills to the position of Virtual Admissions Coordinator with the Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Snider Hockey works to provide students support not just in the game of hockey, but also with their education, postsecondary achievement, and life skills. The ages of the population served range from 4 year’s old to and through their early and mid-twenties and the students are from Philadelphia, Camden, and some suburbs like Pennsauken. After my internship in 2011, I was hired as a part-time coach and in 2012 I was promoted to Site Coordinator of one of Snider Hockey’s 5 main rink locations. In this role, I oversaw hockey, education, and life skills programming. As Site Coordinator I led and trained 15 direct reports with whom I worked to provide programs to 200-500 students each week. In 2016 my responsibilities became more administrative. This seemed to be good timing for me personally as I would no longer be at the rink as much on nights and weekends while my wife and I were planning on having a child. You can find some of my many accomplishments during my time in HR on my resume, but I must admit I always missed working closer with our students.

I was unfortunately let go during Snider Hockey’s 2021 reorganization caused by the pandemic. I actively searched for employment until I was hired as the Assistant Director of Student Records at RCSJ. While in this role for a year and nine months I was supervising the day-to-day operations of the Student Records office and the 2-3 staff members and student workers. I was looking for a role at RCSJ that was more student facing and became an Enrollment Coach and then the Student Affairs Administrator.

While I enjoyed my time at RCSJ I was in search of something more rewarding and felt that my experience and skillset would better serve our community as Student Services Navigator at Atlantic Cape Community College. Unfortunately, they are experiencing budget constraints and decided to not continue my employment at the end of my probationary period.

I was hired by St. John of Go Community Service to be an Employment Specialist in March 2026. I loved working with our clients in this role, however I am in search of a role that better fits the needs of my family.

Thank you for taking the time to read my Cover Letter as well as review my application and resume for the position of Virtual Admissions Coordinator with the Adolescent Wellness Academy. I hope to speak with you or someone on your team in the near future about this opportunity.

Sincerely,
Dennis Cunard

candidates.summary: My experience ranges from retail sales and customer service, to social work in my local community and virtual administrative work for a therapy office located in Virginia. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

My name is Abigail Jane Oporta Morales, and I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position, which I discovered through Indeed. I am particularly interested in this opportunity because of my previous experience working as a translator and interpreter for medical missionary groups, as well as my genuine desire to contribute to adolescent mental health and substance use treatment services.

Throughout my professional experience, I have worked part-time as a translator and interpreter for missionary groups from the United States and South Korea, primarily in the fields of medicine and acupuncture. This experience has allowed me to develop strong communication skills, cultural awareness, and the ability to explain complex information clearly and compassionately. Additionally, I have worked as a personal assistant and website designer, gaining experience in administrative support, website development, and coordinating day-to-day tasks.

My professional background has helped me develop a variety of skills, including teamwork, commitment and reliability, autonomy and initiative, effective communication, organization and planning, time management, attention to detail, meeting coordination and scheduling, and document management. I also have experience making phone calls, following up on communications, and ensuring that tasks and responsibilities are handled efficiently and accurately.

I am particularly drawn to this position because I believe in the importance of helping people feel heard, understood, and supported, especially during challenging moments in their lives. I value providing accurate and helpful information, communicating with empathy, and making sure individuals and their families feel informed and comfortable throughout the admissions process. I am also genuinely interested in your organization’s mission and vision, particularly its commitment to supporting adolescents facing mental health and substance use challenges.

I believe I could bring a combination of strong administrative abilities, effective communication, adaptability, and a compassionate approach to this role. My experience working with people from different backgrounds has taught me the importance of patience, understanding, and professionalism. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute these qualities to your team while supporting adolescents and their families as they navigate the admissions process.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss my qualifications and how I could contribute to your organization in an interview. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,

Abigail Jane Oporta Morales

Sincerely,
Diana Lira

To whom it may concern,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a background in behavioral health, childcare, and remote telephone-based work, I have developed strong communication, organization, and interpersonal skills that I believe would make me a valuable addition to your team.
Through my experience as a behavioral technician and providing ABA therapy, I gained valuable experience working with individuals with behavioral and developmental needs while collaborating with families and maintaining accurate documentation. I worked with individuals looking for a place to start their child’s therapy services and helped them get acquainted to the center. My daycare experience further strengthened my ability to communicate with parents, build trust and relationships, and approach challenging situations with patience, understanding, and compassion. These experiences have given me a strong appreciation for the importance of accessible mental health services and supportive thoughtful care for individuals and families.
Furthermore, my experience working remotely as a telephone interviewer has strengthened my ability to manage phone-based interactions, keep myself motivated, gather sensitive information, maintain accurate records, and communicate professionally with individuals from a variety of backgrounds. I am comfortable working independently, staying organized, managing multiple responsibilities, and maintaining confidentiality when handling personal information.
I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my behavioral health background and communication skills to help individuals and families navigate the process of finding appropriate care. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be overwhelming, and I would take pride in being a compassionate, reassuring first point of contact while helping callers understand their options and next steps.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dependability, and passion for helping others to your admissions team. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how I could contribute to your organization.
Best,
Lyndsey

Dear Hiring Team,

When a parent reaches out because their teenager is struggling, the first voice they hear matters. I would love to be that calm, caring and organized voice for Adolescent Wellness Academy. Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Being the first voice someone hears on one of the hardest days of their life is meaningful work, and I would be honored to meet those callers and families with patience, compassion, and a clear next step.

As a chiropractic receptionist, I worked on the front line of patient care. I scheduled appointments, managed check-ins, processed payments, answered account and billing questions, and handled insurance details. I protected confidential patient and financial records every day, and I understand how much privacy and trust matter in a healthcare setting.

At Pestie, I handled a high volume of inbound calls, emails, texts, and support tickets in a fast-paced environment. I learned to listen carefully, ask the right questions, explain things in plain language, and follow every case through until it was resolved. Many customers reached out frustrated or stressed, and I took pride in calming them down and leaving them with a clear plan.

Here is what I would bring to your admissions team:

• Compassion under pressure: I stay calm, warm, and steady with people who are upset or overwhelmed.

• Strong follow-through: I keep track of every open case and follow up until it is resolved.

• Accuracy and confidentiality: I enter information carefully and handle sensitive records with discretion.

• Clear communication: I explain processes simply and make sure callers know exactly what happens next.

• Quick learning: I pick up new systems quickly and am eager to learn your CRM, EMR, and insurance verification processes.

I also served 19 months as a full-time missionary. I spent much of that time listening to people from every background, many of them going through difficult seasons in their lives, and I learned to meet them with empathy and without judgment. I would bring that same heart to every call. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your families and clients, and I can be reached at (385) 775-4562 or costner195@gmail.com.

Sincerely,

Katie Garn

Dear Hiring Manager,
Thank you for inviting me to share more about my background for the Virtual Admission Coordinator role at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in psychology and hands-on, face-to-face experience caring for patients in my previous role, I know how deeply that very first interaction matters. Being the first voice a teen or parent hears when they reach out for support is a responsibility I take to heart, and I would be honored to bring a calm, warm, and steady presence to your admissions team.
Working directly with patients in person taught me how to read subtle emotional cues, build trust quickly, and stay grounded when families are feeling overwhelmed or vulnerable. Paired with my psychology studies, this experience has given me a strong foundation in adolescent development, active listening, and trauma-informed communication. For many young people and their parents, making that initial phone call is the hardest step they will take. My goal is always to meet them with patience and zero judgment—giving them space to feel heard while smoothly guiding them through the intake process and gathering the details needed to connect them with the right care.

In my previous role, I relied on the exact skills this position requires:
• Warm, Reassuring Communication: Validating concerns and keeping conversations calm, empathetic, and focused during high-stress moments.
• Smooth Intake & Coordination: Listening closely to assess needs, answering questions clearly, and documenting key details accurately without making families feel rushed.
• Composure & Care: Maintaining strict confidentiality, clear boundaries, and genuine kindness throughout busy shifts.

I truly admire Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to making mental health treatment accessible and welcoming for young people and their families, and I would love the chance to speak with you further. Thank you again for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Olivia Deleon

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in opportunities within your addiction treatment program. After several years working in technical and service oriented roles, I am transitioning my career toward the behavioral health field and am currently returning to school to pursue a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology. My longterm goal is to become a Substance Abuse Counselor, and I am seeking a position that will allow me to contribute to a treatment focused environment while gaining direct experience in the field.
Throughout my career, I have developed strong communication skills, disciplined work habits, and the ability to follow structured procedures in high pressure, safety sensitive settings. In my role as an HVACR Technician in commercial food service equipment repairs, I consistently managed complex tasks, documented work with accuracy, and maintained clear communication with customers and internal teams. My experiences have strengthened my ability to stay organized, prioritize effectively, and maintain strong professional standards — skills that directly support operations within treatment facilities.
My background also includes several years of administrative experience, where I handled recordkeeping, scheduling, onboarding support, and general office coordination. This foundation gives me confidence in managing documentation, maintaining confidentiality, and supporting staff and program needs in a clinical or residential setting.
I am committed to building a career in addiction services and am eager to contribute to a team that supports individuals working toward recovery. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills, work ethic, and educational goals align with the needs of your organization.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely, 
Cassius Redmon

Good Morning Hiring Team,

When I saw your opening for a Virtual Admissions Coordinators, I knew I had to apply.

Coming from a family where about 90% of us have struggled with some form of addiction, whether it be alcohol, meth, heroin, cocaine, as well as myself having faced my own battles with addiction, I know this world inside and out. Warmly,

Allison Pokrinchak

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy! As someone with a background in psychology and behavioral health, I’ve always been someone who’s drawn to work that allows me to make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. What particularly caught my attention about this opportunity was the emphasis on being the first point of contact for individuals and families seeking help. I know how overwhelming that first step can be, and I would love the opportunity to help make that process feel a little less intimidating for individuals and families. 

I earned my Bachelor of Science in Psychological and Social Sciences from Pennsylvania State University, where I developed a strong interest in understanding human behavior, mental health, the circumstances that influence an individual’s well-being, and more! That’s why I chose my internship as a Registered Behavior Technician at Helping Hands Family, where I worked directly with individuals receiving behavioral services and collaborated with families and clinical supervisors. Working here taught me that compassion isn’t simply about being understanding; it’s also about being patient, dependable, and recognizing that every individual has different individual needs.

Beyond my behavioral health experience, I bring a strong administrative background. At The Galati Law Firm, I managed sensitive client documentation, coordinated communications, monitored deadlines, and helped clients navigate immigration processes that could often feel very overwhelming. I learned how much of a difference clear communication, organization, and consistent follow-through can make when someone is literally relying on you. 

What drew me to Adolescent Wellness Academy specifically was the opportunity to support adolescents and families during a particularly vulnerable stage of life. I believe that access to mental health care can make a lasting difference, and that the experience someone has when first reaching out for help matters just as much as the steps that follow! I really appreciate that your approach recognizes the importance of meeting individuals with compassion while helping them navigate the more practical aspects of receiving treatment.

I understand that this position requires more than simply answering calls or scheduling appointments. It requires someone who can listen without judgment, someone who can communicate clearly while remaining organized, and someone able to follow through with care AND consistency. These are qualities I have worked to develop throughout my education and professional experiences, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring them to your team!

Thank you for considering my application. I hope to hear back soon! 

Warmly,

Rose Mary Torres

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in a position with adolescent wellness academy. My personal experience in recovery as a mother and as a nurse has provided me with a strong foundation in understanding recovery based inpatient and out patient programs, behavioral health, client care, clinical documentation, and accurate record keeping. I am interested in bringing this experience into an admissions coordinator role where I can continue supporting individuals with recovery and behavioral health needs while utilizing my strengths in organization, communication, and documentation.
Throughout my nursing experience, I worked directly with individuals experiencing a wide range of mental health and behavioral concerns. This role required careful observation, clear communication, and consistent documentation of client needs, behaviors, interventions, medications, and changes in functioning. I understand the importance of maintaining thorough and accurate records, following documentation requirements, protecting confidential information, and ensuring that client records provide other members of the treatment team with the information necessary to maintain continuity of care.
My behavioral health experience has also allowed me to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary treatment teams, communicate client concerns, monitor progress, and assist in coordinating services based on individual needs. Working in psychiatric settings strengthened my ability to remain organized and detail-oriented while managing multiple responsibilities and responding appropriately to changing client needs.
I believe my combination of behavioral health knowledge, direct client experience, and strong documentation and record-keeping skills would translate well to the admissions coordinator position. I understand that successful admissions coordination depends on maintaining organized records, communicating effectively with clients and providers, following through with services and referrals, and ensuring important information is documented accurately and in a timely manner.
I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my recovery and 12 step program understanding and commitment to admissions coordinator position. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills could contribute to your team.
Sincerely,
Cassie Ohl
