candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to express my interest in the Admissions Coordinator opportunity with Adolescents Wellness Academy. My professional background combines healthcare, patient advocacy, community relations, marketing, administration, and relationship building. I believe this combination of experience has equipped me with a unique skill set that would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your organization while supporting adolescents and their families through important and often challenging transitions.

Throughout my career, I have developed strong communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills, along with the ability to navigate sensitive situations with professionalism, compassion, and discretion. My experience as an ER Technician has given me firsthand exposure to patient care, the importance of patient advocacy, healthcare coordination, and the need to make individuals and families feel heard, respected, and supported. Working in an emergency department has strengthened my ability to remain composed under pressure, prioritize competing needs, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, and approach every patient interaction with empathy.

Additionally, my experience as Community Relations and Marketing Director at Goodwill allowed me to develop extensive skills in administration, community partnerships, outreach, public relations, strategic communication, and organizational leadership. I understand the importance of building trust, maintaining professional relationships, managing multiple priorities, and representing an organization with integrity. These experiences translate directly into the responsibilities of an admissions coordinator, from facilitating communication and coordinating processes to creating a welcoming and supportive experience for prospective patients and their families.

What particularly interests me about Adolescents Wellness Academy is the opportunity to combine my healthcare experience with my passion for advocacy and helping individuals access the support and resources they need. I recognize that seeking services for an adolescent can be an emotional and overwhelming experience for families. I would approach every interaction with patience, understanding, professionalism, and a commitment to making the admissions process as seamless and reassuring as possible.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my diverse professional experience, strong administrative abilities, healthcare knowledge, and people-centered approach to your team. I am confident that my ability to connect with people while balancing the operational demands of an organization would make me a valuable addition to Adolescents Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and enthusiasm could contribute to your organization’s mission.

Brie Osmon

Although I do not have direct experience in behavioral health admissions or substance use treatment intake, and my professional background has not included a fully remote position, I am confident that many of my existing skills would transfer well into this role. I am always eager to learn and would welcome the opportunity to expand my experience in a field that aligns closely with my professional interests.

candidates.cover_letter:
Good Afternoon:

My name is Rebecca Brogan and I wanted to take a moment to introduce myself.  I am currently seeking a new remote position where I can use my skills and talents.  I believe my education and work experience would make me a great fit for this position.

I have my Bachelors in Social Work degree and the majority of my experience is in skilled nursing, assisted living, and homecare.  I have worked as an Activity Director on an interdisciplinary care plan team, developing individualized plans of care for residents in skilled nursing facilities, assisting in admission and discharge planning, and resolving grievances.  I was also responsible for educating the residents about their rights and assisting them by researching possibilities that would help them meet their needs.  I planned and implemented both group and individual activity programming to meet their psychosocial needs.  I assisted them in the care of their activities of daily living as both a CNA and Activity Director.  I completed my BSW internship in a 2-1-1 call center where I assisted callers with problem solving, researched appropriate options and explained how to reach out for assistance.  The call center also served as the suicide hotline for the local area, and during those crisis calls I used the RIDE model and other counselling models to help deescalate the situation and offer support to the caller.   Upon graduation, I worked in a home care office where I recruited, screened, qualified, onboarded, trained, scheduled, and helped to retain a team of over 300 caregivers while also helping to ensure the overall office ran efficiently.

Recently I have had to take some time off due to health and family challenges and I am ready to return to work.  I am empathetic, professional, and a multi-tasker who enjoys challenges.  I have experience working with diverse populations and extensive experience with clients with challenging behaviors and managing difficult situations.  I am a quick study and able to adapt my skills to new situations and circumstances.

I would love to be able to be a part of your team.

Thank you for your consideration and I hope to hear from you soon.

Sincerely,
Rebecca Brogan

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. My professional background includes substantial experience in behavioral health, patient support, and healthcare coordination, and I believe my experience aligns well with the needs of your admissions team.

In my previous roles with UnitedHealthcare/Optum, I worked directly with patients and members navigating healthcare needs, including behavioral health-related services and support. What draws me to this position is the opportunity to make a meaningful difference at the very beginning of someone’s treatment journey. Whether speaking with an individual seeking substance use treatment or a parent looking for mental health support for their teenager, I believe the first interaction matters. I would bring compassion, professionalism, strong communication skills, and a genuine commitment to helping people take the next step toward care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to your team.

Sincerely, Kara Sakurai.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I’ve seen how difficult it can be for families to find adolescent mental health and substance use treatment when they need it. In my current role at Eliot Community Human Services, I help families and DCF teams navigate that process, from clarifying what support a young person needs to following up with providers when a referral stalls.

As a Family Networks Service Coordinator, I manage referrals and follow-up across approximately 120 cases, including referrals to intensive outpatient programs. I gather referral information, contact providers about availability and intake requirements, and track outstanding steps so families and referring teams know what to expect. When a program cannot accept a referral, I clarify the barrier and help identify another option. I’d bring that same follow-through to helping families move from their first call through admission.

Previously, as a Therapeutic Trainer on an in-home therapy team at Embrace Pathways, I worked directly with youth and caregivers facing behavioral health challenges, including families affected by substance use. That experience taught me how to build rapport in difficult moments, explain unfamiliar processes in plain language, and give families space to ask questions. I also hold a master’s degree in Community Social Psychology.

I’d welcome the opportunity to bring my experience with adolescent behavioral health referrals and family support to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for considering my application.

Best,  
Elizabeth Estrela

To Whom it May Concern,

I am writing to express my interest in opportunities within your organization. With a Bachelor of Science in Public Health from San Diego State University and a Master of Public Health from the University of South Florida, I have developed a strong foundation in health services, community outreach, and addressing barriers that prevent individuals from accessing essential resources. I am eager to apply my educational background, administrative experience, and interpersonal skills in a role where I can contribute to organizational goals while making a meaningful impact on the individuals and communities served.

In my recent role as a Client Coordinator at NewLeaf Peer2Peer, I gained extensive experience coordinating services, maintaining accurate records, verifying insurance eligibility, and facilitating communication among clients, clinicians, and interpreters. This position required strong organizational skills, attention to detail, discretion, and the ability to manage competing priorities while working with sensitive information. I regularly assisted individuals in navigating administrative processes, resolving service-related concerns, and connecting with appropriate resources. These responsibilities strengthened my ability to manage daily operations, communicate effectively across multiple teams, and ensure tasks were completed accurately and efficiently.

My public health education and additional professional experiences have further strengthened my ability to work with individuals from diverse backgrounds and contribute to community-centered initiatives. As a Peer Health Educator at San Diego State University, I developed educational materials, facilitated workshops, provided resource referrals, and collaborated with health professionals and community partners. Through my volunteer work with the Tampa/Hillsborough Reproductive Well-Being Learning Collaborative, I also contributed to community outreach initiatives, analyzed quantitative and qualitative information, and helped develop recommendations to improve access to services. These experiences reinforced the importance of effective communication, collaboration, and understanding the unique needs of the populations an organization serves.

I would bring strong written and verbal communication skills, technological proficiency, and the ability to adapt to new systems, policies, and procedures. I am comfortable reviewing detailed information, organizing documentation, managing multiple responsibilities, and maintaining confidentiality when handling sensitive records. I also value opportunities for professional development and continuous learning, and I approach new responsibilities with initiative, flexibility, and a willingness to grow.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my skills, experience, and educational background to your organization. I believe my combination of public health knowledge, administrative experience, and commitment to improving the well-being of others would allow me to make a valuable contribution to your team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and experiences align with your organization's needs.

Sincerely,
Ashley Hacker

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the remote Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 10 years of experience in healthcare, behavioral health support, and consumer relations, I specialize in guiding individuals and families through sensitive, high-stress decisions with warmth, clarity, and urgency. I deeply admire Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to providing compassionate, specialized mental health and substance use care for teens, and I would be honored to serve as a supportive first point of contact for your families.
Reaching out for adolescent treatment is often one of the most overwhelming moments a parent or guardian will ever face. Serving as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator requires more than administrative precision—it demands active listening, genuine empathy, and the ability to build immediate trust over the phone or screen. Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in these exact areas:
• Empathetic Family & Client Rapport: Experienced in de-escalating crisis moments, listening without judgment, and reassuring anxious parents and caregivers while clearly explaining program options and next steps.
• Seamless Intake & Insurance Navigation: Skilled at conducting thorough initial assessments, verifying insurance benefits accurately, coordinating with clinical teams for level-of-care approvals, and maintaining strict HIPAA compliance in a remote environment.
• Persistent, Organized Follow-Through: Proven ability to manage a high volume of inquiries in CRM and EHR systems, ensuring timely follow-ups so no teen or family falls through the cracks during the critical window between first contact and admission.
Working remotely requires strong self-direction and seamless communication with multidisciplinary teams. My background bridging front-line support and healthcare administration allows me to collaborate effortlessly with clinicians, utilization review specialists, and outreach teams to ensure every transition into care is as smooth and stress-free as possible.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my dedication to behavioral health advocacy, rapport building, and admissions coordination can help Adolescent Wellness Academy connect more teens and families with life-changing care. I can be reached at 812-653-6468 or richardsonfancy@gmail.com to schedule an interview.  

With Gratitude 
Nancy M Richardson

candidates.cover_letter:
Hello,

I'm excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am drawn to this opportunity because it combines compassionate communication, organization, and the ability to make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families seeking support. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership, customer service, and interpersonal communication experience to your team.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong ability to connect with people, understand their needs, and provide thoughtful assistance in fast-paced environments. Most recently, I have worked with the Mt. Lebanon Extended Day Program, where I previously served as Center Director and now continue as a Staff Member. In this role, I have been responsible for maintaining a safe and supportive environment for children, coordinating programming, supervising staff, and ensuring that organizational policies are consistently followed. Working closely with children and families has reinforced the importance of patience, empathy, reliability, and clear communication.

My previous experience as a Customer Experience Manager at Michaels further strengthened my ability to manage daily operations, coach employees, resolve concerns, and ensure that every individual receives attentive and professional service. I also have experience as a Front Desk Attendant, where I served as an initial point of contact, welcomed visitors, answered questions, and helped create a positive first impression. These experiences have taught me the importance of listening carefully, communicating clearly, and following through to ensure that people's needs are addressed.

Additionally, my experience as a Peer Writing Tutor provided valuable training in active listening and reflective communication. Through a four-month training program, I developed skills in understanding individual perspectives, asking thoughtful questions, and guiding others through challenging situations. I believe these skills would translate well to speaking with prospective clients and families who may be navigating difficult or emotional circumstances.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming experience. I would conduct every interaction with compassion, professionalism, and respect, recognizing the importance of making each caller feel heard and helping them understand their next steps. I'm highly organized, adaptable, comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, and committed to providing consistent, high-quality service.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, communication skills, and commitment to helping others could contribute to the admissions teams at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I look forward speaking with you.

Thank you,

Cassidy Higgins

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a strong background in healthcare administration, admissions management, patient access, and care coordination, I bring the experience and interpersonal skills necessary to support individuals and families as they navigate the admissions process.

My experience has strengthened my ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate records, communicate with sensitivity, and work collaboratively with clinical and administrative teams.

I understand that seeking support for an adolescent can be an emotional and sometimes overwhelming experience for families. I would bring a family-centered approach to every interaction while ensuring that inquiries, referrals, follow-ups, and admissions responsibilities are handled efficiently and accurately.

Additionally, my experience with healthcare systems, electronic documentation, insurance processes, and patient coordination has prepared me to work effectively in a virtual environment. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my admissions experience, organizational strengths, and passion for helping individuals and families to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to your team and mission.

Sincerely,

Rian Washington

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and extensive experience in behavioral health, substance use treatment, case management, and remote administrative services, I bring the compassion, communication skills, and organizational abilities necessary to support individuals and families seeking treatment.

During my employment as a Probation and Parole Agent with the State of Wisconsin, I gained valuable experience working remotely while independently managing a demanding caseload, conducting client assessments, coordinating services, maintaining confidential documentation, and communicating with individuals facing complex mental health and substance use challenges. This experience strengthened my ability to remain organized, prioritize responsibilities, and provide professional, compassionate support without requiring constant supervision.

Previously, as a Substance Abuse/Mental Health Case Manager with Sheboygan County and a Drug Treatment Court Case Manager with JusticePoint, I worked directly with individuals seeking behavioral health and substance use services. My responsibilities included assessing referrals, determining eligibility and treatment needs, coordinating with providers, and helping clients navigate available resources. Additionally, my experience as a Virtual Assistant strengthened my ability to manage incoming calls, respond to inquiries, coordinate appointments, maintain accurate records, and communicate effectively in a remote environment. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, confidentiality, and ensuring that individuals receive clear information and appropriate next steps.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because I understand how overwhelming seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be for individuals and their families. I would welcome the opportunity to serve as a compassionate first point of contact, helping callers feel heard, supported, and confident as they begin their treatment journey.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health background, remote work experience with the State of Wisconsin, and commitment to helping others align with the needs of your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Hayley A. Garlow

I have hands-on experience working as a Social Worker and Supervised Visitation Supervisor, supporting children and families involved in the child welfare and family court systems. My responsibilities include conducting client intakes, coordinating and supervising court-ordered parent-child visitations, maintaining detailed case documentation, and ensuring a safe, structured, and supportive environment for families.

I have experience working with families navigating complex circumstances, including child removal, custody disputes, family conflict, and court involvement. I closely monitor parent-child interactions, assess observable behaviors, document emotional responses, and evaluate parents' ability to demonstrate appropriate caregiving, communication, and parenting skills.

My role requires strong observational skills, crisis management, conflict resolution, and the ability to remain professional and impartial in emotionally sensitive situations. I prepare comprehensive, objective visitation reports, maintain confidential client records, communicate with caregivers and involved professionals, and ensure compliance with court orders and agency policies.

Additionally, I handle administrative responsibilities such as scheduling appointments, coordinating visits, managing case files, completing intake documentation, and maintaining accurate records. Through this work, I have developed strong skills in case management, family advocacy, professional documentation, trauma-informed communication, and supporting the safety and well-being of vulnerable children and families.

work_history.title: Social Worker Supervisor
work_history.summary: Social Services Supervisor / Supervised Visitation Specialist Job Responsibilities and Duties Responsible for coordinating, supervising, and documenting court-ordered and agency-referred parent-child visitation services for families involved with Child Protective Services (CPS), the Department of Human Services (DHS), and the family court system. Work directly with parents whose children have been removed from their custody due to concerns involving abuse, neglect, substance use, domestic violence, or other circumstances affecting child safety and welfare. Provide professional oversight of family interactions while maintaining a safe, structured, and supportive environment that promotes healthy parent-child relationships and supports family reunification efforts when appropriate. Client Intake and Case Management * Conduct comprehensive client intake interviews with parents, guardians, and other individuals referred for supervised visitation services. * Review court orders, agency referrals, custody arrangements, safety plans, and relevant case documentation to establish visitation requirements and restrictions. * Gather and maintain confidential client information, including family histories, contact information, case circumstances, visitation goals, and identified safety concerns. * Explain program policies, visitation expectations, confidentiality requirements, behavioral guidelines, and consequences of noncompliance to participating families. * Assess individual family needs and identify potential barriers to successful visitation, including transportation difficulties, communication challenges, and scheduling conflicts. * Coordinate initial visitation arrangements between parents, caregivers, caseworkers, attorneys, and other involved parties. * Maintain organized client records and monitor ongoing compliance with court-ordered visitation requirements. Supervised Parent-Child Visitation * Provide direct, in-person supervision of court-ordered parent-child visits in community settings, including public parks, recreational facilities, restaurants, museums, shopping centers, and other approved locations. * Monitor interactions between parents and children to ensure physical safety, emotional well-being, and compliance with established visitation guidelines. * Observe and objectively assess parental behaviors, communication patterns, emotional responsiveness, discipline techniques, and the ability to recognize and respond appropriately to children's needs. * Document children's observable emotional responses, behavioral changes, verbal statements, and interactions with their parents throughout scheduled visits. * Monitor parental engagement, including the ability to provide appropriate supervision, establish healthy boundaries, demonstrate affection, and participate in age-appropriate activities. * Intervene when necessary to address inappropriate behavior, safety concerns, violations of visitation guidelines, or situations that could negatively affect a child's well-being. * Facilitate safe transitions between custodial caregivers and visiting parents while minimizing conflict and maintaining professional neutrality. * Recognize and respond appropriately to signs of emotional distress, potential abuse, neglect, or other child welfare concerns. * Maintain professional boundaries and impartiality while working with families experiencing complex interpersonal, legal, and emotional circumstances. Documentation, Reporting, and Case Notes * Prepare detailed, objective, and comprehensive visitation reports documenting parent-child interactions, behavioral observations, significant statements, and notable incidents. * Record children's demeanor upon arrival, emotional responses throughout visitation, and behavior during departure and separation from visiting parents. * Document parental caregiving behaviors, responsiveness to children's needs, verbal communication, physical affection, and ability to maintain appropriate boundaries. * Maintain accurate records of visitation dates, locations, attendance, arrival and departure times, cancellations, and compliance with court-ordered conditions. * Prepare factual incident reports concerning safety violations, inappropriate conduct, emotional distress, or other significant occurrences requiring additional documentation. * Distinguish direct observations from statements made by parents, children, caregivers, or third parties to ensure accurate and unbiased reporting. * Complete case notes and administrative documentation within established deadlines. * Maintain confidential records in accordance with organizational policies, applicable privacy requirements, and professional documentation standards. * Provide visitation reports and relevant case information to authorized caseworkers, legal representatives, courts, and other designated professionals as required. Administrative and Operational Responsibilities * Coordinate and manage visitation schedules for multiple families while accommodating court requirements, client availability, and approved community locations. * Communicate professionally with parents, custodial caregivers, caseworkers, attorneys, and agency representatives regarding scheduling, visitation requirements, and case-related concerns. * Maintain client files, intake paperwork, consent forms, visitation records, incident documentation, and other administrative materials. * Track completed visits, missed appointments, cancellations, rescheduling requests, and service-related communications. * Ensure documentation is properly organized, accurate, and submitted according to established organizational procedures. * Assist with resolving scheduling conflicts, communication difficulties, and logistical issues that may interfere with visitation services. * Monitor adherence to agency policies, court orders, safety protocols, and professional standards. * Manage multiple active cases simultaneously while prioritizing child safety, timely reporting, and effective communication. * Exercise independent judgment in community-based environments when responding to unexpected circumstances, behavioral concerns, or potential safety risks. Child Welfare, Safety, and Professional Responsibilities * Prioritize the physical and emotional safety of children involved in court-ordered visitation services. * Maintain awareness of child development, trauma-informed practices, family dynamics, and the effects of separation and family instability on children. * Identify and document observable indicators of potential maltreatment, emotional distress, or unmet basic needs. * Follow applicable mandatory reporting requirements when suspected child abuse or neglect is identified. * Apply de-escalation and conflict-resolution techniques when managing emotionally charged interactions between family members. * Maintain neutrality, professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality when working with sensitive family situations. * Support opportunities for positive parent-child interaction while ensuring all contact remains consistent with court orders and established safety guidelines. * Collaborate with involved professionals to support continuity of services and accurate communication regarding family visitation. Overall Position Summary Serve as a community-based supervised visitation professional responsible for client intake, case coordination, direct supervision of court-ordered parent-child contact, comprehensive behavioral documentation, and administrative case management. Work with families involved in child welfare proceedings, including cases where children have been removed from parental custody, to ensure visitation occurs in a safe, structured, and professionally monitored environment. Balance independent fieldwork, detailed reporting, confidential recordkeeping, communication with multidisciplinary professionals, and adherence to court-mandated requirements while maintaining a child-centered, objective, and trauma-informed approach.

Jermiane Rodriguez
New Braunfels,Texas
Jermrazorod@icloud.com
(210) 917-7557

November 17, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Human and Community Advocacy from the University of Texas at San Antonio, an Associate of Arts in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare, customer service, and public assistance, I bring a combination of professional qualifications, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping adolescents and families access mental health services.

Throughout my career, including my work with Texas Health and Human Services, healthcare-related call centers, and my current position with Aflac, I have developed strong skills in communication, active listening, documentation, problem-solving, and assisting individuals through complex and sometimes emotionally challenging situations. My experience has taught me the importance of maintaining confidentiality, gathering accurate information, explaining processes clearly, and ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported.

What makes this opportunity particularly meaningful to me is my personal experience as a mother who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for a child experiencing significant emotional and behavioral health challenges. I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to mental health advocacy would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jermiane Rodriguez

Hiring Team

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in behavioral health support, community services, remote administrative coordination, and client focused communication, along with a B.A. in Psychology, I am passionate about helping individuals and families navigate the process of accessing meaningful mental health and recovery support.

This experience reinforced the importance of meeting people with compassion, patience, and respect, particularly when they are navigating difficult circumstances or seeking support for the first time. I understand that accessing behavioral health services can feel overwhelming, and I believe the initial interaction can play an important role in helping someone feel comfortable, understood, and encouraged to take the next step.

My experience as a Remote Administrative Assistant with the National Acupuncture Detoxification Association further strengthened my ability to manage scheduling, data entry, reporting, and administrative responsibilities in a remote environment. Additionally, my work with Volunteers of America involved maintaining confidential client information, verifying records, and supporting documentation and reporting needs. These experiences have strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage administrative responsibilities while maintaining confidentiality and professionalism.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it combines my educational background in mental health, my experience supporting individuals within community based services, and my interest in making behavioral healthcare more accessible. I would welcome the opportunity to help prospective clients and families understand their options, coordinate next steps, maintain consistent communication, and experience a supportive and organized admissions process. I am also eager to continue developing my knowledge of admissions workflows, insurance coordination, and electronic healthcare systems while contributing to a team committed to helping individuals and families find care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my compassion, communication skills, administrative experience, and commitment to supporting others to your team.

Sincerely,
Courtney Evans

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Remote Mental Health Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background spanning healthcare, education, and public service, I bring a unique combination of compassionate communication, organizational skills, and experience supporting individuals and families through challenging circumstances.

Throughout my career, I have been drawn to positions that allow me to make a meaningful difference in the lives of others. As a Lead CNA and Medication Technician, I learned the importance of providing patient-centered care, maintaining confidentiality, and approaching sensitive situations with empathy and professionalism. I am organized, dependable, attentive to detail, and comfortable balancing multiple responsibilities while maintaining a supportive and professional approach. I would welcome the opportunity to apply these strengths in a remote admissions setting, helping families navigate their options and take meaningful steps toward receiving the care they need.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy's work supporting adolescents and families on their journey toward healing and recovery.

Sincerely
McKenna Valdivia

Adolescent Wellness Academy’s family-centered approach and commitment to expanding access to treatment for adolescents strongly resonate with me. RE: Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, residential services, and program operations, I bring a strong background in leadership, staff development, clinical coordination, and quality improvement. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute my experience to a growing program focused on improving access to mental health services for adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have held progressively responsible positions, including Behavioral Health Program Manager and Coordinator, overseeing daily operations across multiple outpatient services. In these roles, I supervised more than 21 employees, coordinated multidisciplinary teams, monitored program productivity and spending, and supported operational improvements to strengthen service delivery. My experience also includes admissions coordination, community referrals, staff scheduling, documentation oversight, and maintaining compliance with Medicaid, DCF, CARF, and HIPAA requirements.

My professional background has allowed me to develop a strong understanding of the importance of balancing clinical quality with operational efficiency. I recognize that building a successful program requires more than providing services. It involves developing strong referral relationships, supporting staff, monitoring performance, identifying opportunities for growth, and ensuring that individuals and families receive timely, coordinated care.

Although much of my recent clinical and operational experience has focused on adults with mental health and co-occurring substance use disorders, my earlier experience providing behavioral support services has strengthened my understanding of individualized care, family collaboration, and the importance of early intervention. I believe these experiences provide a valuable foundation for supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy's family-centered approach to adolescent treatment.

I have completed all requirements for my Master of Social Work degree through Walden University and am awaiting official degree conferral. I also hold the Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager Supervisor (CBHCMS) credential and have submitted my application for Florida Registered Clinical Social Work Intern registration. These professional milestones reflect my continued commitment to clinical development, ethical practice, and effective behavioral health leadership.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, operational knowledge, and commitment to quality care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to the continued development of its Virtual IOP through strong team leadership, community partnerships, and a consistent focus on program performance and client outcomes.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional goals align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Michelle Antonia Rivera

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health background, leadership capabilities, and business education to support effective program operations, strengthen community partnerships, and advance positive outcomes for the adolescents and families you serve.

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Operations Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. What particularly attracted me to this opportunity is the chance to be part of a founding team and help establish a supportive, well-organized environment for adolescents and their families. With a Master’s degree in Counselling Psychology, two years of full-time experience working directly with mental health clients, and a background in operations management, staff supervision, and business administration, I believe I can bring a valuable combination of clinical understanding and operational leadership to your new North Carolina location.

As the founder of HAP TherapyCare, I independently established and managed a virtual psychotherapy practice while providing direct mental health services. Beyond working with clients, I was responsible for nearly every aspect of running the practice, including client inquiries, intake, scheduling, billing, clinical documentation, professional referrals, and maintaining appropriate standards of confidentiality and care. This experience gave me an appreciation for how much the quality of a client’s experience depends on what happens behind the scenes. Clear communication, reliable processes, timely follow-up, and a welcoming environment can make a meaningful difference for individuals and families seeking support.

My operational leadership experience extends beyond healthcare. At Toronto Inspection Ltd., I coordinated 10 to 15 field technicians and more than 20 daily site visits across multiple active projects while guiding administrative staff, resolving escalations, and improving documentation processes. I regularly investigated complex operational and billing discrepancies, worked with different stakeholders to identify solutions, and introduced practical improvements to make daily operations more organized and efficient. I also bring experience in employee recruitment, interviewing, onboarding, training, and supervision, along with additional business administration and payroll responsibilities through my work with Saphgen.

One quality I would particularly bring to Adolescent Wellness Academy is a strong sense of ownership. When something is not working, I naturally want to understand why, explore possible solutions, and follow through until the issue is addressed. I enjoy creating structure, supporting colleagues, and finding ways to make people’s work easier without losing sight of the individuals we serve. My counselling background has also shaped how I lead and communicate, with empathy, patience, accountability, and respect for different perspectives.

I understand that launching a new behavioral health clinic requires flexibility, collaboration, and attention to both operational details and the experiences of clients, families, and staff. Although I have not previously managed an adolescent PHP or IOP program, I am eager to build on my existing experience, learn the specific requirements of your programs, and contribute to establishing strong operational foundations from the beginning.

Sincerely,
Hareesma Amutha Venkatesan

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy as you prepare to open your first North Carolina clinic. What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to be part of something that can make a genuine difference in the lives of young people and their families. Throughout my career, I have found the most rewarding part of my work is knowing that what I do has a meaningful impact on someone else's life. That is something I experienced firsthand at Shine Support Services, and it is something I hope to continue in my next role.

At Shine Support Services, I helped build the Supportive Employment Program from the ground up. I operated and developed workflows, internal procedures, training materials, participant resources, and documentation standards to help establish the foundation for daily operations. More importantly, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, support their goals, and build relationships with their families and community partners. I loved being able to see the difference that consistent support and encouragement could make in someone's confidence, independence, and everyday life. I taught a coping skills class that incorporated Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) practices, giving participants the opportunity to learn and practice healthy coping strategies. Those experiences reminded me that meaningful progress is not always one big milestone. Sometimes it is the smaller moments of growth that make the work so worthwhile.

I also bring leadership and operational experience from Graphic Components, where I led the photopolymer department before being promoted to Project Manager. I coordinated departmental workflow, monitored quality, addressed production challenges, developed procedures and training documentation, and cross-trained employees and prospective hires. This experience strengthened my ability to organize competing priorities, support a team, solve problems, and create systems that help people do their jobs effectively.

My experience working with young people also extends to YPATC, a youth performing arts program in Florida, where my responsibilities ranged from scheduling appointments to teaching theater to children. I enjoyed being part of an environment where I could contribute both behind the scenes and directly to the experiences of young people. I have pursued the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training coursework, further developing my understanding of behavioral support and different learning and support needs.

What draws me to AWA is the opportunity to bring these experiences together in a setting where the work has such an important purpose. I understand that a successful program depends on more than the services being offered. It also takes thoughtful organization, dependable staff, clear communication, consistent routines, and an environment where young people and their families feel supported. I would be excited to help build that foundation for AWA's North Carolina clinic.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, leadership, and passion for meaningful work could contribute to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Sincerely,

Erica R. Warriner

My background in developing and implementing therapeutic programs allows me to bridge the gap between clinical requirements and the emotional needs of diverse populations, from pediatric patients to seniors.

Throughout my career, I have prioritized collaboration as a cornerstone of my clinical practice. While working with interdisciplinary teams at Miami Jewish Health and Fort Lauderdale Behavioral Health, I successfully led therapeutic initiatives that fostered physical and emotional recovery. By integrating medical play, guided imagery, and personalized treatment plans, I have effectively helped patients manage pain and anxiety, consistently representing their perspectives to ensure comprehensive care delivery.

My approach is rooted in diligent planning and proactive problem solving. Whether assessing the needs of at-risk youth or supporting families facing complex medical challenges, I focus on adapting interventions to maximize therapeutic outcomes. My foundational knowledge in exercise science and rehabilitation therapy provides me with a versatile clinical toolkit that I am eager to apply in a new professional setting where patient-centered care is the priority.

I am confident that my clinical expertise and commitment to evidence-based recreation therapy would make me a valuable asset to your team. I appreciate your time and consideration of my background, and I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my experience aligns with your current needs.

Sincerely,
GODIVA SIMEON

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the part-time Operations Support Specialist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am currently completing my Bachelor's degree in Psychology at Florida International University and am interested in gaining further experience within a behavioral health environment. I was drawn to this opportunity because of AWA's commitment to creating a supportive, welcoming, and structured environment for adolescents and their families.

Through my internship at My Optimal Child, I gained experience in a behavioral health setting, where I assisted with administrative and organizational responsibilities, prepared materials, organized documents, and had the opportunity to observe therapists working with children, teens, and families. This experience helped me develop a greater understanding of the importance of maintaining an organized and supportive environment in a behavioral health practice.

Additionally, I have several years of babysitting experience, which has strengthened my ability to demonstrate patience, take responsibility, and create a safe and positive environment for children. I consider myself dependable, and willing to take initiative wherever help is needed.
I would be excited to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy by helping maintain a clean, organized, and welcoming facility while supporting the daily operations of the program. I believe my educational background, previous experience, and genuine interest in working in behavioral health would make me a strong addition to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my qualifications further and look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,

 Anna Babinchak
